quotes.text: The problem isn't the AI tool, it's the operating model around it. Leaders often can't answer a few basic questions who owns this agent? What data can it reach?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames why an AI CoE is an operating-model question, not a tool question.

quotes.text: The goal isn't to treat every use case like a major software release. The goal is to match the review to the risk.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise principle for risk-based AI governance.

quotes.text: An agent doesn't become safe because it worked in a demo. It becomes safer because people know exactly when to step in.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Strong argument for human oversight of agents.

quotes.text: AI can search and summarize much faster, so weak permissions become easier to notice. AI didn't create that access problem. It brought the problem into view.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains Copilot oversharing risk without blaming the AI.

quotes.text: Training must include judgment, not just prompts. People need to verify output, check the source, protect sensitive data, and recognize when AI isn't the right tool for the job.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical guidance for AI adoption training.

takeaways: An AI Center of Excellence is a cross-functional team and repeatable way of working that turns scattered Copilot, Power Platform and Azure AI experiments into owned, controlled work.
Governance should match the review to the risk: low-risk drafting gets a fast path, while agents that act on people, money or sensitive data need deeper review and human oversight.
Start small: inventory every AI tool, agent and flow, name an owner and data source for each, and send one measurable low-risk use case through a simple intake path.
hook: Copilot pilots, low-code agents and Azure AI apps are spreading faster than most organizations can track who owns them or what data they reach. This episode explains the Microsoft AI Center of Excellence for IT leaders, security teams and adoption owners, built on three pillars: governance, security and adoption. You will get a practical first 90-day plan for scaling AI safely.
